correctness.rationale: The normalized evaluation columns have two ring components differing by q_m=(-1)^(l+m) exp(i*pi*m/N). DFT residue blocks have eigenvalues 2N times positive alias sums, with q_(m+N)/q_m=(-1)^(N+1). The Gegenbauer coefficient ratio has odd denominator, and the leading term at reduced even-denominator c uniquely minimizes the two-adic valuation for every derivative of P_l; all amplitudes are positive. Residue counts give the asserted sharp ranks. Independent symbolic rational and numerical Gram checks cover 130 cases and 2520 amplitude instances, supplementing rather than replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted public research-record searches and material inspection of three relevant primary open-access texts found no identical all-N, all-degree exact two-ring Gram spectrum or parity-sharp full-rank threshold. The closest earlier results are full-bandlimit or multi-ring polynomial interpolation, not the same fixed two-ring exact-degree evaluation. Residual historical equivalence risk remains; standard DFT, addition theorem and arithmetic nonvanishing technique are not claimed as new.
residual_risks: An older harmonic interpolation table, dihedral representation result or textbook Fourier aliasing theorem may contain an equivalent block-spectrum classification under another formulation.
The result is a closed exact classification on a natural configuration, not a claim of a fundamentally new Fourier principle; its novelty is the full quantified spectral/rank synthesis.
Uniform stability or extension to odd reduced denominators was not established.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-degree, all-order classification of the singular-value spectrum for a natural and practically relevant paired-latitude sampling geometry, across a dense family of eligible heights. It determines the exact attainable data dimension and sharp interpolation threshold and identifies a parity switch between an antipodal rank ceiling and unrestricted full rank. This answers intrinsic exact-degree spectral interpolation questions beyond a finite table; no downstream global theorem is asserted. In contrast to generic-point arguments at a fixed degree, one explicit arithmetic height condition works simultaneously for every degree, yielding a dense deterministic family of maximally unisolvent fixed geometries.
